claim: Free-form stochastic local search on the exact R (randomized coordinate hill-climbing / bumps / gaussian blobs) beats every parametric family tried: from the constant start (R=2/3) it reached 0.8237 (p0002, N=48), 0.7879 (p0003, N=80), and 0.8370 (p0004, N=400), all far above the two-level bath's 0.6667 (p0005) and the symmetric coordinate search's 0.7236 (p0007). The best profiles are strongly as

The symmetric two-level edge-boost bath (height A on first/last k of N=2000, 1 in the middle) gave no gain over the constant function: R stayed at 0.666667 (p0005). The edge-boost picture alone does not flatten f*f enough; the optimum is not a symmetric U-shape.

Two separated rectangular blocks (widths w1,w2, gap g, height ratio r) beat the constant start substantially: R=0.796296 (p0006), with f*f having 40% of knots within 0.1% of its maximum (a near-plateau) and peak at 0.5. This shows a gap between blocks is a productive mechanism for flattening f*f, though it is still below free-form search.

Symmetric free-form coordinate search (N=201, mirror-symmetric heights, multiplicative perturbations) reached only 0.723584 (p0007), well below the asymmetric stochastic searches (0.82-0.84). Imposing symmetry on the profile is a real handicap; the best profiles found are asymmetric.

Higher R correlates with a flatter f*f top and a shifted peak: the best result (p0004, R=0.837) has 7.6%/25.0%/38.3% of f*f knots within 0.1%/1%/5% of max with peak at 0.334, versus the constant's 0.12%/1.02%/5.02% at 0.5. Flattening f*f (raising the 1% and 5% shares) while keeping ||f*f||_inf low is the operative lever.

Does increasing resolution help? p0004 used N=400 and scored highest (0.8370) while p0002 (N=48) scored 0.8237 and p0003 (N=80) 0.7879, but these differ in search method too. Worth testing: fix the best search and sweep N to see whether finer discretization reliably raises R, and whether the asymmetric multi-block/edge structure persists at large N.

Coordinate-descent sweeps plus structural mutations (insert/delete/perturb steps) on the raw heights beat random single-index hill-climbing: from p0002's 0.823732 it reached 0.844878 at N=48 (+0.021146), with 20.6%/33.0%/39.2% of f*f knots within 0.1%/1%/5% of max and peak at 0.396. Systematic sweeps exploit the smooth dependence of R on each height better than random index picks.

Per-coordinate adaptive (1+1)-ES with the 1/5 success rule at N=800 gave essentially no gain over p0004: 0.837134 vs 0.837037 (+0.000097) in the full 30 s budget. Adaptive per-coordinate step sizes do not escape p0004's basin; the bottleneck is the basin, not the step-scale schedule.

K-block parameterization (K=2..6, free breakpoints and heights, differential evolution + Nelder-Mead + coordinate polish) returned exactly p0004's start value 0.837037 (+0.000000): the few-block family could not improve on the pixelwise solution, so a simple asymmetric multi-block step function is not a better basin than p0004's free-form shape.

The incremental O(N) convolution update for single-coordinate changes crashed with a broadcast error (shapes (1200,), (2400,), (1200,)) at the shift-add step, so the N=1200/2400 polish never ran. The intended update L += delta*(shift(h,i)+shift(h,-i)) + delta^2*e_{2i} was mis-implemented; the resolution question (F6) remains untested under a fixed good search.

Raising the symmetric half-vector search from N=201 to N=401 with multiplicative coordinate hill-climbing and kicks gave no gain: 0.723620 vs 0.723584 (+0.000036). Finer grid alone does not fix the symmetric parameterization's deficit versus asymmetric searches (0.72 vs 0.84).

Does resolution help once the search method is held fixed? p0004 (N=400, 0.8370) and p0010 (N=800, 0.8371) differ only modestly in resolution and score nearly identically, while p0012's N=48 coordinate-descent run reached 0.8449 — suggesting search strategy, not grid size, dominates. Worth testing: same coordinate-descent/structural-mutation search swept over N in {48, 100, 200, 400, 800}.

Replacing p0012's fixed ±step coordinate trials with exact bounded 1-D maximization per coordinate (scipy minimize_scalar over [0, 4*old]) raised R from 0.844878 to 0.845012 (+0.000134) at N=48, and shifted the f*f peak from 0.396 to 0.219 while keeping the flat top (0.1%-of-max knot share 20.62% -> 21.65%). The gain is real but tiny: the ±step sweeps were already near-optimal per coordinate, so t

Upsampling p0012's best N=48 shape to N=96/192/384 and rerunning the same coordinate+structural search gave exactly 0.844878 (+0.000000): the multi-resolution phase never improved on the N=48 start. Finer grids do not help once the search method is fixed, consistent with F12's hint that N=48 is already sufficient.

Plateau-guided step insertion (splitting a step where f*f is within 2% of its max) plus smallest-diff merges gave no gain over p0012: R stayed at 0.844878 (+0.000000), with the 0.1%-of-max knot share unchanged at 20.62% and peak still at 0.396. Inserting degrees of freedom where the plateau already is does not flatten it further; the plateau is limited by the global shape, not local resolution.

Analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B ascent plus backtracking polish and upsampled coordinate descent at N=1200 gave only +0.000082 over p0008 (0.837037 -> 0.837119). The gradient route is efficient but lands on the same plateau: 0.1%-of-max knot share 7.25% vs p0004's 7.6%, peak at 0.421. Gradient ascent does not beat stochastic coordinate search at this resolution.

A coarse K=400 control grid scored on a 20000-step upsampled array, with block/smooth kicks and fine polish, reached only 0.724048 (+0.000464 over p0007's 0.723584). The symmetric parameterization remains stuck near 0.724 regardless of resolution (N=20000 here vs N=201/401 before), confirming that symmetry itself, not grid fineness, caps this family.

Adding smooth Gaussian/cosine bump families and multi-mode stochastic hill-climbing with restarts to the two-block family raised R from 0.796296 to 0.802069 (+0.005772) at N=100, with a flatter f*f top (0.1%-of-max knot share 15.42%, peak at 0.510). Smooth bumps beat pure rectangles but still trail free-form asymmetric searches (0.82-0.845).

Replacing the non-smooth max L in R by a p-norm surrogate ||L||_p and running a continuation (p=4,8,16,32,64, ~2s each) before exact-R coordinate sweeps and mutations raised R from 0.845012 to 0.878060 (+0.033049) at N=46: the largest single gain since the free-form searches, with the f*f top much flatter (0.1%-of-max knot share 21.65% -> 33.33%) and the peak moved to 0.543. Smoothing the max lets

Joint adjacent-pair optimization (alternating exact 1-D maximization on h[i], h[i+1] for each pair, 3 rounds) added after p0017's single-coordinate sweeps gave only +0.000008 (0.845012 -> 0.845020) at N=48. Correlated pairwise moves do not escape the single-coordinate local maximum; the plateau is not a pairwise-coordinate artifact.

Symmetry-broken upsampling (each N=48 height split into two with ±10% random perturbations, then the same coordinate sweeps and mutations at N=96) gave only +0.000015 (0.845012 -> 0.845027) and returned an N=48 shape. Breaking the upsampling symmetry does not make higher resolution pay off under the exact-coordinate search.

Multi-resolution resampling (96/160/128/64 steps with exact coordinate re-polishing after each) gave only +0.000009 (0.845012 -> 0.845021) and returned the N=48 shape. Resampling across scales does not escape the single-resolution local optimum.

Replacing scipy minimize_scalar with a coarse-then-fine grid line search per coordinate plus multi-op basin hopping with incumbent deep-polish gave only +0.000004 (0.844878 -> 0.844882) at N=48. Faster line search and basin hopping do not beat exact bounded 1-D maximization; the plateau is not a line-search precision issue.

The p-norm continuation (p0024, 0.878060) is the only lever that moved the score materially this generation. Worth testing: sweep the p schedule (more values, longer per-p budget, higher final p), apply the continuation to the N=48 p0017 shape vs. other starts, and combine it with structural mutations at higher N. Making the p-norm continuation denser and convergence-driven (p=4..384, each stage run until surrogate gain <1e-9, 65% of budget) gave no gain over p0024: R stayed at 0.878060 (+0.000000) at N=46 with identical f*f statistics (33.33% of knots within 0.1% of max, peak at 0.543). Converging each surrogate stage more thoroughly does not move the basin; the 0.878 shape is a fixed point of the continua

Letting step structure co-evolve under the smooth objective (insert/delete/perturb structural moves inside the p=8/16/32 stages, ~1.5 s per stage) gave no gain over p0024: R stayed at 0.878060 (+0.000000), N unchanged at 46. Structural moves under the smoothed objective are either rejected or neutral; the step count does not grow during continuation.

Starting the p-continuation from deterministic spiky analytic profiles (power-law exponents, tent, jittered copy at N=64, each given an even time slice) did not beat p0024: best final R was 0.878060 (+0.000000), N=46, same f*f profile (33.33% within 0.1% of max, peak 0.543). Hand-built spiky starts do not reach or improve the 0.878 basin within the continuation budget.

Adding analytic reverse-mode gradient ascent through the convolution plus a smoothing mutation between coordinate sweeps (p0026) returned exactly p0024's score 0.878060 (+0.000000) despite changing the shape (N=36, max/mean 5.40, 42.47% of knots within 0.1% of max, peak at 0.403). The gradient route lands on a different shape with the same R, confirming the 0.878 level is a plateau rather than a s

The analytic-gradient rewrite of p0024 crashed with NameError: name 'den' is not defined (gradient expression used den before assignment, only gden defined), so the golden-section + gradient variant never ran. Any future analytic-gradient polish must define the denominator before forming (gnum*den - num*gden)/den^2.

On the two-block/bump family, adding a resolution-mutation move plus a wider resolution sweep and tighter xatol raised R from 0.802069 to 0.803713 (+0.001645) at N=80 (down from 100), with a flatter f*f top (13.66% of knots within 0.1% of max vs the family's prior level, peak at 0.331). Doubling the resolution of the 0.878 basin by repeating each height twice (N=46 -> N=88) and rerunning the identical p-norm continuation (p=4..64, 2.5 s/stage) plus exact polish raised R from 0.878060 to 0.878083 (+0.000023), the only gain this generation; the f*f top flattened (0.1%-of-max knot share 33.33% at both, but 1% share 36.56% -> 38.98%) and the peak moved from 0.543 to 0.511. The gain i

Eight random heavy-tailed spiky multi-starts (N in {40,45,50,55,60}, 30% zeros, exp(1.5*N(0,1)) heights) run through the p-norm continuation before the base polish gave no gain over p0024: R stayed at 0.878060 (+0.000000), N=46, identical f*f stats (33.33%/36.56%/37.63%, peak 0.543). Random restarts do not find a better basin than the 0.878 one within the budget.

Replacing the p-norm surrogate with a softmax/log-sum-exp surrogate (beta=1..64 continuation) gave exactly p0024's score 0.878060 (+0.000000) with identical shape (N=46, max/mean 6.90, peak 0.543). The specific polynomial weighting of the p-norm is not the bottleneck; a different smooth-max family lands on the same optimum.

Adding a p-norm smoothed-max continuation plus a peak-duplication mutation to the N=48 coordinate-descent search (p0020 base) gave only +0.000059 (0.844882 -> 0.844941). The p-norm continuation that gave +0.033 from the 0.845 start in p0024 does not reproduce that jump when grafted onto this variant; the gain depends on the specific base/search, not the surrogate alone.

Multi-resolution starts (2x upsample, downsample) plus a smoothed-max continuation phase and an extra mutation operator gave only +0.000001 (0.845027 -> 0.845028) at N=48, with f*f stats essentially unchanged (0.1% share 21.65%, peak 0.469). Resampling across scales does not escape the N=48 local optimum.

Dropping the multi-start continuation and instead heavily polishing the incoming 0.878 start with coordinate descent plus insert/delete/perturb/smooth mutations returned exactly 0.878060 (+0.000000) but at a different shape (N=36, max/mean 5.40, 0.1%-of-max knot share 42.47%, peak 0.458). The 0.878 score is reachable by several distinct shapes, so shape statistics alone do not identify the optimum
